heard: Millions of invisible black holes are silently prowling our galaxy. Astronomers recently detected the first confirmed rogue stellar mass black hole wandering entirely alone through space. Astronomers spotted it when its intense gravity magnified and bent a distant star's light. Hubble tracked the shifting starlight over six years to pinpoint the invisible traveler. Data from 16 different ground-based telescopes helped confirm the phantom weighs 7.15 solar masses. This dark remnant is approximately 5,000 light-years away and emits zero detectable light. It was hurled through space at 51.1 kilometers per second by a massive supernova kick. The confirmed existence of this phantom suggests that a terrifying number of them remain unseen.
